reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the ExampleScenario StructureDefinition report, the local R4/R6 element shapes, the direct SearchParameters behavior finding affecting ExampleScenario, and the shared Resource/DomainResource behavior context. I formed the resource-level judgment before comparing it to the deterministic aggregate; shared base behavior was treated as context only.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 ExampleScenario was trial-use/FMM 0, so the compatibility burden is weak and broad redesign is easier to justify than it would be for mature clinical or infrastructure resources. That does not erase the practical fact that existing instances need transformation, nor does it make low-cost compatibility preservation valueless.

overall.oneLineConclusion: ExampleScenario keeps its resource identity, but R6 remodels the actor, instance, operation, workflow, and validation model enough that real R4 instances require a resource-level migration program.

reasoning.thesisMd: This is not a removed resource, but it is a same-name major remodel. The repeated replacement of R4 identifiers and labels with R6 `key`/`title` pairs, generalized instance typing, operation restructuring, workflow relocation, and new internal-reference invariants means a syntactic version bump or validator update is not enough. Because the R4 artifact was FMM 0, most of the redesign looks proportionate, but specific low-cost preservation opportunities still deserve attention.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The dominant migration shape is a whole-resource model transformation. Actors move from `actorId`/optional `name` to required `key`/`title`; instances move from `resourceId`/`resourceType`/optional `name` to `key`/`structureType`/required `title`; version and contained-instance references are renamed; operation number/name/type are redistributed into step number, required operation title, and Coding type; root workflow links move into step workflow context; and R6 validators add uniqueness, completeness, mutual-exclusion, and internal-reference rules. These changes affect the resource's core scenario graph rather than isolated optional metadata.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: A migration program is already unavoidable for implementations that store or exchange non-trivial ExampleScenario instances. That lowers the leverage of preserving every old wire name, especially given FMM 0 and the risk of keeping duplicate obsolete and new representations in the base model. It does not imply that additional avoidable breaks are irrelevant: preserving deprecated aliases or transition metadata where it is cheap can still reduce conformance, tooling, and manual-review cost.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: Most field-level redesigns are local migration chores once the R6 model direction is accepted; keeping every old actor, instance, version, and operation field in parallel would create duplicate representations and ambiguous precedence rules. The workflow change is different because R4 root `workflow` links can require semantic placement into a specific step; a deprecated root-level transition field, alias, or explicit computable migration convention may be worth standards review. The direct SearchParameter canonical consolidation also has a plausible low-cost less-breaking path: publish or advertise deprecated per-resource canonical aliases while retaining the normalized multi-base definitions.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: The only direct behavior finding for ExampleScenario is the SearchParameter canonical consolidation. Runtime query strings are mostly preserved, but conformance identity changes can break CapabilityStatement comparison, generator registries, and tests that key search support by canonical URL; that remains worth follow-up despite the resource's structural migration burden. The 11 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings are relevant environmental context for any ExampleScenario endpoint, but they are not resource-specific evidence because ExampleScenario is neither Resource nor DomainResource.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: The deterministic aggregate concluded `Yes` for major migration, `major-model-remodel`, and `preserve-where-low-cost-but-expect-resource-migration`. I agree with that conclusion, but for substantive reasons rather than counts alone: the core scenario graph is remodeled and validated differently, while the workflow and SearchParameter findings still retain avoidable-compatibility value.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: Real-world deployment prevalence is uncertain because R4 ExampleScenario is FMM 0/trial-use. The exact design rationale and full terminology expansion context for the actor-type vocabulary were not in the local inputs, but the structural evidence is sufficient for a high-confidence resource-level migration judgment.

findingConsiderations.title: Actor identifier/name fields were replaced by key/title, with title now required
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Actor identity and rendering labels are core to ExampleScenario diagrams. R4 `actorId`/`name` instances are not directly R6-valid and R6 requires `key`/`title`, so this is a hard transformation for almost any useful scenario. Given FMM 0 and the coherent R6 key/title pattern, it is mainly evidence of the broader remodel rather than an independently high-leverage preservation target.

findingConsiderations.title: Actor type binding changed from ExampleScenario person/entity to ActorDefinition person/system/collective/other
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The required binding change makes R4 `entity` invalid without mapping, so it is a real instance break. It is localized and likely manageable through an explicit code map, but it should not be missed because the path name stayed the same.

findingConsiderations.title: Instance declarations were remodeled from resourceId/resourceType/name to key/structureType/title
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is central to the resource's payload: examples being exchanged are no longer modeled as FHIR-resource-specific `resourceId`/`resourceType` records, but as generalized keyed structures with required titles. That requires model-aware migration and can affect generated APIs, stored data, and scenario rendering.

findingConsiderations.title: Instance version and contained-instance references were renamed and retitled
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The version and contained-instance changes extend the same key/title remodel into the reference graph. Because request/response content can depend on these internal references, migration must preserve referential integrity rather than simply rename fields.

findingConsiderations.title: Operation number/name/type were replaced by step number, required operation title, and Coding type
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Operation rendering and typing are part of the scenario flow. Moving the number to the step, requiring an operation title, and changing primitive operation type to Coding are hard validation and codegen changes that reinforce that a whole-resource transformer is needed.

findingConsiderations.title: Workflow nesting moved from root workflow to step.workflow and nested process cardinality narrowed
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the structure finding with the strongest avoidability concern. Moving root `workflow` into a specific step can require semantic placement judgment, and narrowing nested process repetitions may require splitting or choosing among actions. Even though the resource needs migration anyway, a transition design for old root workflow links could avoid unnecessary manual review.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds local invariants for completeness, uniqueness, mutual exclusion, and internal references
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The new invariants are hard validator behavior, but they largely enforce consistency expected by the remodeled key/reference graph. They matter for migration test planning after structural transforms, yet they do not by themselves change the resource-level posture.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds optional content that is not losslessly representable in R4
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is primarily R6-to-R4 downgrade loss from optional new content, not an R4-to-R6 hard instance break. It should inform bidirectional converter policy but does not drive the forward migration conclusion.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 consolidates many per-resource canonical SearchParameter URLs into multi-base CanonicalResource and MetadataResource definitions
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This direct behavior finding affects ExampleScenario's conformance surface even though runtime query codes are largely preserved. Canonical URL identity is commonly used by CapabilityStatement comparison, client generators, and conformance tests, and deprecated aliases appear to be a low-cost compatibility-preserving option.

findingConsiderations.title: Resource $meta-add is removed from R6 core
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This can affect generic Resource endpoint behavior for ExampleScenario instances, but it is shared base Resource behavior rather than an ExampleScenario-specific model change, so it was not counted in the resource-level migration shape.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Treat ExampleScenario migration as a whole-resource transformation with validation after conversion, not as independent field renames. Migration guidance should cover key/title generation, actor type mapping, operation type Coding creation, workflow placement, and post-transform invariant checks.

Revisit the workflow relocation break specifically. Consider a deprecated root `workflow` transition path, explicit computable mapping rules, or normative migration guidance to avoid avoidable manual placement work.
For the affected canonical SearchParameters, consider deprecated per-resource canonical aliases or clear equivalence metadata so R4 conformance tooling can bridge to the R6 multi-base definitions.

caveats: Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were reviewed only as context because ExampleScenario is not one of those base artifacts.
R4 FMM 0/trial-use means real implementation prevalence is uncertain and weakens the standards burden to preserve every old element name.
The local inputs did not include full committee rationale for the ExampleScenario remodel or full terminology expansion details for the actor-type change.
